question: Can the three fixed-heavy planar-H failures be rescued by minimal local heavy-atom geometry repair or full restrained relaxation, without silently changing topology or the raw model?
scope: Complete preparation of six saved raw PDBs: three rejected plus three compatible controls. Not neural inference or repertoire throughput. Same parent R8 H geometry, pH7, protonation variants and disulfides. 3 workers, two fresh containers per policy and route; reversed order in replicate2.

policies.local_policy: Only preflight failures move heavy atoms. Radius1 ksteric100000, followed on explicit gate failure by radius2 ksteric500000, each from original coordinates. kpos10000, bond x10, angle x10, preserve strained noncore valence. CPU1.
policies.restrained_policy: Only preflight failures: full-heavy geometry prepass, physical fixed-heavy H minimisation, CUDA mixed full Amber ff14SB/GBn2 plus kpos1000 anchored original and biological chirality wall1e8; max3000; require convergence; final H uses same R8 policy.
policies.gates: Original motif bonds <=0.05 A, angle <=10 degrees from ff14SB; no new heavy bond errors >0.10 A, angle errors >20 degrees, severe heavy contact pairs <0.7*(vdW radius sum) excluding <=3 bond neighbours; no true CA/ILE/THR inversions. Final independent stored-PDB H/planarity/topology and Probe checks follow timings.
policies.ram_scope: Host MemAvailable at 20ms, 5s pre idle median, 8s post. Additional unavailable memory includes host noise/cache; post drift and baseline sensitivity reported. No summed RSS+CUDA.
policies.selection: Development-selected three failures, not independent accuracy holdout. No reference experimental structure. No main/dev setting changed.
